Overall this is looking really good! 

> - In abstracting the vertex shader code into the vertex_shader() function, the new function seems unable to take an argument of type SceneData. Whenever trying to do this, the shader breaks and I receive VK_ERROR_UNKNOWN. To work around this, I am instead passing all of the needed, individual fields from the SceneData structs. This makes for a very long function signature and I'd like to change it if possible.
> 
> - In scene_forward_mobile.glsl, the y values of prev_screen_position/screen_position need to be flipped, but they need to be flipped after they are passed to gl_Position in the vertex shader. Without flipping them, the color output of the motion vectors texture is incorrect. But if y is flipped earlier, the position is incorrect. Currently this is solved by flipping the y at the end of the fragment shader when calculating ndc coordinates, but this feels a bit hacky to me. Does anyone have ideas on how else this could be accomplished?

Both of these sound very fishy. For the first one my guess is its an Adreno driver bug :( Did you get the same error when running on desktop?

For the second one, I suspect that the extension is requesting MVs in a forward backwards from our own. FSR2 has an option to tell the plugin what range the MVs are in, does Application space warp have something similar? Ideally we would render MVs with the same format that we do in the rest of the engine and then trust the plugin to scale them as needed.

I've realized that the issue of passing the `SceneData` into the `vertex_shader()` function is actually an issue of accessing multiview data with `ViewIndex` inside `vertex_shader()`.  The function signature now takes a `SceneData` struct and the three multiview parameters required to work around this. I encountered a similar problem in the compatibility renderer PR with multiview data in the scene shader: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/97151

Then, some notes about motion vectors in general with space warp. It would seem that space warp motion vectors live in a [-2, 2] NDC type space, multiplying the NDC values by 0.5 before subtraction causes obvious space warp artifacts. Per the [space warp spec](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenXR/specs/1.1/html/xrspec.html#XR_FB_space_warp):
> The motion vector data is stored in the `motionVectorSubImage`’s RGB channels, defined in NDC (normalized device coordinates) space, for example, the same surface point’s NDC is PrevNDC in previous frame, CurrNDC in current frame, then the motion vector value is "highp vec3 motionVector = ( CurrNDC - PrevNDC ).xyz;".

The current output to the motion vector textures is what I would expect for space warp. Here are some screenshots from renderdoc. Stationary headset, the top two cubes are moving to the right (positive X direction) while the other two are moving upward (positive Y). These two textures appear to line up exactly (or at least as close as they can, since the MV texture is much lower resolution).

While this PR works great for me on the Meta Quest, there appear to be some serious performance and stability issues when testing on my Samsung S21 Ultra.

I ran the modified TPS Demo from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/90284 with the `debug/settings/stdout/print_gpu_profile` project setting enabled, and on master (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/aef0065e090bb4ed0b75c6e2e576e0ef26020a5d) I get around 50 mspf; with this PR, I'm getting around 600 mspf. So, it's >10x slower :-/

Moreover, with this PR, it will crash after about 20 seconds. Strangely, I don't get a backtrace or any of the usual information in the logs with the crash, so it may not actually be crash, but the process being killed by the OS?

I'll spend some more time trying to narrow down the issue...

After some experimentation, it looks like copying the `SceneData` struct is what's causing the performance issues on my Samsung S21 Ultra. It's not just passing it as an argument - I tried copying the contents of the `vertex_shader()` function into `main()`, and just having a `SceneData scene_data = scene_data_block.data` in there would cause the performance issues.

With [this patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20444919/pr-100283-perf-fixes.patch.txt) the performance goes back to normal on my phone, and AppSW still works fine on the Meta Quest.

I don't know that the changes in my patch are _good_ changes, though. It works by passing the individual fields as arguments into `vertex_shader()`, which won't be the most fun to maintain. There's probably other ways it could be done? Like, maybe we could make a smaller struct and maybe passing that into the function wouldn't have the same issues? Or, if the uniform had an array of `SceneData` structs, and then we could just pass the index into `vertex_shader()`?

I'd love to know if there is a preferred way to work around this!
@dsnopek Thank you for finding and addressing the issue! I've applied the patch with a little tweak since the shader was failing to compile for the editor. 🙂

Now that the big difference is fixed, I've done some more in-depth benchmarking on my Samsung S21 Ultra using the modified TPS Demo from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/90284.

Here are the frame times from master (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/aef0065e090bb4ed0b75c6e2e576e0ef26020a5d):

| Run | Mean | Median |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 51.76 mspf | 50.80 mspf |
| 2 | 52.53 mspf | 50.87 mspf |
| 3 | 51.80 mspf | 50.78 mspf |

And here are the frame times from this PR:

| Run | Mean | Median |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 51.45 mspf | 50.70 mspf |
| 2 | 50.66 mspf | 50.65 mspf |
| 3 | 50.65 mspf | 50.63 mspf |

The runs with the PR came out _slightly_ faster, but I'm assuming that's normal variation, and the performance is effectively the same.

I gathered them by enabling the `debug/settings/stdout/print_gpu_profile` project setting, then grabbing the times from `adb logcat` and using a Python script to average them. I let each run go for about 60 seconds.

Between each run, I waited 5 minutes for the phone to cool down. Otherwise, each run would be slower than the previous one (even for the exact same build). I'm assuming this is due to thermal throttling, but I couldn't find a way to disable it on a non-rooted phone.

In an attempt to ensure more consistent results, I also ran these `adb` commands and disabled "Power saving" mode in the phone's UI:

<details>
<summary>Pre-test `adb` commands</summary>

```bash
# Disable doze and app standby.
adb shell dumpsys deviceidle disable
adb shell settings put global device_idle_constants inactive_to=9999999,sensing_to=9999999,locating_to=9999999,location_mode=disabled

# Keep the CPU awake and the screen on.
adb shell svc power stayon true
adb shell settings put system screen_off_timeout 2147483647

# Limit background processes.
adb shell settings put global background_process_limit 0
```
</details>

For completeness, here is my Python script:

<details>
<summary>Python script for processing times from log</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python

import re
import sys
from statistics import mean, median

def extract_frame_times(lines):
    times = []
    pattern = re.compile(r'GPU PROFILE \(total ([0-9.]+)ms\):')
    for line in lines:
        match = pattern.search(line)
        if match:
            times.append(float(match.group(1)))
    return times

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) > 1:
        with open(sys.argv[1], 'r') as f:
            lines = f.readlines()
    else:
        lines = sys.stdin.readlines()

    times = extract_frame_times(lines)
    if times:
        print("Median frame time:", median(times), "ms")
        print("Mean frame time:", mean(times), "ms")
        print("Total times:", len(times))
    else:
        print("No frame times found.")
```
</details>

> Between each run, I waited 5 minutes for the phone to cool down. Otherwise, each run would be slower than the previous one (even for the exact same build). I'm assuming this is due to thermal throttling, but I couldn't find a way to disable it on a non-rooted phone.

You can get an active cooler to prevent that, or if you don't have one, put the phone in front of a desk fan using a stand.
